text: To falter is to become weak or unsteady. Here, if any part of the chain from brain to muscle falters, your grip gets weaker.
Taxing means very tiring and hard work. Getting 39 muscles to team up is hard work for the brain.
To foreshadow is to give an early hint of something coming. A weak grip may hint at memory and thinking trouble later.
"Get a grip" is a saying that means calm down and take control of yourself. The article plays with it, because people are now literally working on their grip.
An idiom is a saying whose meaning is different from its separate words, like "break a leg."
A dead hang is an exercise where you hold onto a bar and dangle with your arms straight, as long as you can.
A farmer's carry is an exercise where you walk while holding something heavy in each hand, like buckets of water.
A hand gripper is a small spring tool that you squeeze to make your hand stronger.
A trigger is something that sets off a chain of events, like a spark. Here, one famous study set off the trend.
Headline-grabbing means so surprising or exciting that newspapers print it in big letters.
The Lancet is a famous medical journal, a magazine where doctors and scientists publish their studies.
Associated means connected or linked. When a study says two things are associated, they tend to show up together.
Cardiovascular means having to do with the heart and the blood vessels that carry blood around the body.
Systolic blood pressure is the pressure of blood pushing on your artery walls each time your heart beats. Doctors measure it to check your health.
A predictor is a clue that helps you guess what will happen next, like dark clouds predicting rain.
Alas is an old-fashioned word that means unfortunately. It shows the writer is a little sad about what comes next.
A puppet is a toy that moves only when someone pulls its strings. The scientist means muscles move only when the brain tells them to.
A physiologist is a scientist who studies how living bodies work, such as how muscles and hearts do their jobs.
Neurological means having to do with nerves and the brain, the body's wiring and control center.
A chain of command is the order in which orders are passed down, like from a coach to the captain to the team. Here, orders pass from the brain through nerves to muscles.
Electrical signals are tiny zaps of electricity that carry messages along your nerves between your brain and body.
Nerves are thin, wire-like parts of your body that carry messages between your brain and the rest of you.
Orchestration means organizing many parts so they work together, like a conductor leading an orchestra. Here, the brain leads the hand muscles.
To muster something is to gather it up, like courage or strength. Here, it is the force each finger can gather.
A cognitive test checks how well your brain thinks, remembers, and solves problems.
Cognitive decline means thinking and memory slowly getting worse, which can happen as people get very old.
Intriguing means so interesting that it makes you want to know more.
An early warning is a sign that tells you about a problem before it gets big, like a smoke alarm.
A meta-analysis is a study of studies. Researchers combine the results of many earlier studies to find a clearer answer.
An observational study watches what happens to people without telling them what to do. It cannot prove one thing causes another.
A follow-up period is how long researchers keep checking on the same people after a study starts.
Asymmetry means two sides that are not equal. Grip asymmetry means one hand is stronger than the other.
Your dominant hand is the one you use most and are best with, such as your right hand if you are right-handed.
Telling here means revealing or showing something important, not talking. A telling gap is one that gives a clue.
A cohort study follows a group of people over many years to see who gets sick and who stays healthy.
To pool things is to put them together into one big group, like pooling money. Here, nine studies were combined.
Neuromuscular means having to do with nerves and muscles working together.
A hemisphere is one half of something round. Your brain has a left and a right hemisphere.
Division of labour means splitting up jobs so different parts do different tasks. Here, each side of the brain handles one hand.
Deterioration means slowly getting worse over time.
A word of caution is a warning not to take something too far. The writer says not to read too much into grip strength.
A diagnosis is a doctor's decision about what illness a person has.
Warranted means deserved or called for. Here, more checks are a good idea.
Resistance training is exercise that makes muscles push against weight or force, like lifting weights or doing push-ups.
"Hang in there" means keep going and do not give up. It is also a joke here, because hanging is a grip exercise.
